project: Function Vectors in Large Language Models

CS1.name: Conclusion vs Original Results
CS1.description: Check if all evaluable conclusions in the documentation/plan match the results in the code implementation
CS1.rationale: All documented results in plan.md are consistent with the ICLR 2024 paper (documentation.pdf). The plan contains specific numerical results (e.g., GPT-J+FV achieves 90.8% shuffled-label accuracy vs 39.1% baseline, 57.5% zero-shot vs 5.5% baseline) that match the paper's reported figures. The code implements experiments that generate these results dynamically rather than storing hardcoded values, which is appropriate for reproducibility.

CS2.name: Implementation Follows the Plan
CS2.description: Check if all plan steps have corresponding implementations
CS2.rationale: The plan describes 6 experiments, but only 5 have corresponding implementations. Experiment 3 (Vector algebra composition) is missing from the codebase. This experiment involves testing whether algebraic sums of function vectors can execute combined tasks (e.g., Last-Capitalize, Last-Country-Capital, Last-Antonym), but no implementation code was found.

missing_implementations.plan_description: Test vector algebra composition by constructing decomposable tasks and measuring whether algebraic sums of FVs can execute combined tasks
missing_implementations.expected_functionality: Extract FVs for individual tasks (e.g., Last, Country-Capital), perform vector arithmetic (v*BD = vB + vD - vI), evaluate composed vectors on composite tasks
missing_implementations.files_searched: All .py files in src/ directory and notebooks/

summary.overall_assessment: Partial consistency. Documented conclusions match the paper results (CS1 PASS), but implementation is incomplete with 1 of 6 planned experiments missing (CS2 FAIL).
